hook.text: 188 countries follow the Codex Alimentarius—a food code that sets global standards for safety, labeling, and trade.

buildup.text: Created by WHO and FAO in 1963, Codex develops international food standards to protect health and ensure fair trade.

discovery.text: Codex standards are not legally binding. But the WTO uses them to settle trade disputes—effectively making them global law.

twist.text: Countries can set stricter standards than Codex but must scientifically justify them. The EU often does; the US sometimes does.

climax.text: Codex sets pesticide residue limits, additive caps, and hygiene codes used by developing nations building regulations.

punchline.text: One global food code, 188 countries, voluntary but trade-enforced. Codex rules quietly.

quiz.question: How does the Codex Alimentarius become effectively binding?
options: The WTO uses Codex standards to settle international trade disputes
